now: The hunt's fight is visible: `encounter` steps `battle.stepper` one turn every `config.turnSteps` sim steps, emits a `battle:strike` per blow, calls the move out over the trainer and the wild, and a fainted lead is replaced mid-duel rather than ending it. A wiped party pays a tenth of the wallet and is taken to the Pokemon Center. Ether and Max Ether exist, a Potion no longer revives, and one ball per defeated wild is a named rule (DECISIONS #72). The production build now carries its sprite art and the gate asserts it, and exactly one thing runs the hunt at a time - visible is `encounter`, hidden is `idle`, and the encounter counter changes hands at the edge. Nothing appears from nowhere any more: the tall-grass step roll is deleted everywhere and the city spawns nothing. The rest of phases B-E of the brief - targeting, the stash/bag split and per-species loot, the five missing automations, and the move VFX - are not started.

baseline.note: demo city at noon. Real numbers, but the scene has no buildings, no NPCs and no characters yet.

open.what: **A found circuit does not visit the places the biome composes.** Measured in the meadow: the loop is a 6x17 corridor at x 38-43, 50 cells of a 64x60 map, and the campfire that is its only night practical is at (25,32) — 14 cells away, with the `lane` marker 23. So a hunt is walked in a corner the player never sees composed. Invisible until now because `biome.walk` stages every showcase and preset at the markers instead: every hunt frame ever judged shows a part of the map the game does not walk.

`biome.walk` — the pre-loop scripted routes — is still read by `stageWalk` and by `showcase.js`. Two ways to move a party through a biome, one of them superseded. Deleting it was tried and reverted in the same session: with one route, the meadow's night frame loses its practical entirely (`over200Pct 1.198 -> 0`), because of the circuit-placement defect above. The deletion is correct and lands after the circuit does.

`stepDuel`'s `between` and `nextAlly` hooks are wired but stubbed: `between` is always empty and `nextAlly` takes the next conscious member in party order. Auto-Heal, Auto-Ether, Auto-Revive and the matchup-aware lead are the rules that belong there (brief, phase D).

`useItem()` still has zero consumers. The duel applies items through `battle.applyAction` on a combatant record, not on a `pokemon` instance, so the intent object it returns has no caller and the manual-use path is still unbuilt.

The lead is not chosen for the matchup: a Water starter walks into a Grass wood, and the faint-swap takes the next party member in line rather than the right one. The move-priority list makes this addressable by a player; the automation still does not do it. (DECISIONS #70(j))
`pacing.js MEASURED` projects an income model that DECISIONS #69 deleted. The table is stale and the header (`pacing.js:22`) says so. (DECISIONS #70(j))
Slots thin as the circuit bends: 9 at four corners, 5 at twenty, because a bent ring has fewer cells at Chebyshev 2 that are not already path.
The coast circuit runs through inland grass rather than along the shoreline -- the bend heuristic prefers path/tallgrass, and the shore is neither.
`go()` is serialised but not cancellable: once a scene starts building, the player waits for it.
Travelling mid-encounter calls `encounter.cancel()` with no prompt. A silent loss of a fight the player was in.
Accuracy and evasion stages are not modelled -- deliberate, and stated at `stats.js:41`. Only the five battle stats stage.

Daylight frames have no motivated light source, which is what four rounds of blind A/B judging lost on every time. Night and cave frames, which have practicals, win. See `docs/STATUS-ARCHIVE.json` -> gate.blindJudging.
